text:
Gavin McKenna is 18, the first overall pick, and playing for a Maple Leafs team that has lost nine of the last ten games he has dressed for. That's the frame for everything else. Fourteen points in 23 games, six of them goals, is a good rookie line: the median top-three pick since 2005 managed 0.55 points a game in his first full season, and McKenna is ahead of that, though behind the 0.9 that Connor Bedard and Macklin Celebrini posted.

Half his points have come on the power play, which is why the debate over his spot there matters; former NHLer Matthew Barnaby has argued, per The Leafs Nation, that he should be back on the top unit. Five-on-five is harder going: Toronto gets 42% of the expected goals with him on the ice, and he plays under 14 minutes a night. The skating is already elite, with a top speed in the league's 97th percentile.

Tuesday's first meeting with Bedard, who praised him beforehand, ended in a 6-3 loss in Chicago, with McKenna adding an assist. The rookie numbers are fine. How much rope Toronto gives him is the story to follow.
headline: McKenna is producing on a team that keeps losing
